TITLE: Planned fuel duty rise to be scrapped, says Keir Starmer
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-20 11:36 (updated 13:39)
AUTHOR: Peter Walker
SOURCE: The Guardian

KEY:
- Starmer announced at PMQs: extending temporary 5p fuel duty cut for rest of year
- 12-month vehicle tax HOLIDAY for hauliers
- Cost ~£400m; Reeves will set out details Thursday
- Treasury: by end of 2026, freeze will have saved average driver £120 over two years
- 1-year vehicle excise duty pause saves £600 for typical heavy lorry
- 5p cut first introduced by Rishi Sunak in 2022 after Russia invasion of Ukraine
- At last budget Reeves announced 9-month fuel duty freeze + 5p cut ending September
- Treasury hasn't clarified if full 5p increase will go ahead January

STARMER QUOTES:
- Asked by Labour MP Kirsteen Sullivan about cost-of-living measures: "There is more that we can do, and I can announce today that we are giving our hauliers a 12-month vehicle tax holiday, helping to keep prices down, and we are backing drivers by extending the freeze in fuel duty for the rest of the year"
- "This is possible because of the decisions taken by the chancellor, making us the fastest-growing economy in the G7"
- "This is not our war, but while the parties opposite wanted to jump into it, Labour will always protect working people"
- To Badenoch claiming U-turn: "I know the leader of the opposition likes to claim responsibility for things that have got literally nothing to do with her. In her mind, she won Eurovision on Saturday and scored the winning goal in the FA Cup final"

REEVES QUOTE (Treasury release):
- "The war in Iran is pushing up fuel prices here at home but after strong growth at the beginning of the year, I am stepping in to protect people at the pump"
- "By protecting households and businesses we are building a stronger and more secure economy for Britain. That is the right economic plan"

BADENOCH:
- Sought to claim credit for the decision, saying it was a U-turn caused by her pressure
